text:
Nina_ml: quick heads-up — I swapped in the fp8-vec kernel on a Mistral-7B quant profile this morning. End-to-end P95 latency is up ~7% and KV hit-rate dropped from 0.82 -> 0.71 with the same workload. Not sure if the kernel changed the KV copy/layout or if batching interacts badly. Anyone else seeing this?

Sam_g: yep, saw something very similar on Qwen-7B last week when we rolled fp8 vectorized kernels. Profiling summary from a local run: overall kv_hit 0.78 -> 0.66 after kernel swap. Sequence length dist was skewed (short prefixes high): 8:45%, 64:35%, 256:20%.

Sam_g: command I used to reproduce:
```
./runtest --model=mistral-7b --profile=fp8-mixed --kernel=fp8-vec --batch=8 --kv-cache=true --trace=kv_stats.txt
```
and kv_stats.txt snippet:
```
KV_HIT: 0.71
KV_MISS: 0.29
KV_COPY_MS: 1.6
P95_LAT_MS: 54.3
```

Olga_infra: @Nina @Sam can you confirm if this only happens when batch>1? We recently changed batching stride handling and saw index offsets when memcpy alignment differs between kernels. Also, paste the quant layout in the model config (how the KV tensors are packed).

Sam_g: tested batch=1 vs batch=8: batch=1 hit=0.80, batch=8 hit=0.68. So batching amplifies misses with the fp8-vec kernel. Hypothesis: the vectorized kernel does a 32-byte-aligned KV copy that, when used with our batching stride, leads to shifted keys for some prefix lengths.

Nina_ml: repro + minimal workaround I tried: force fallback to int8 for prefixes <64 with this patch: `runtime.force_kernel=int8 if prefix_len<64`. After that p95 returned to baseline and hitrate recovered to ~0.81. Quality delta was negligible in our eval.

Kevin_perf: we should add this to the perf regression tracker and publish a small remediation: route short-prefix traffic to INT8 kernels until we fix alignment in fp8-vec. Filing a report: https://internal/reports/1918765432-kv-fp8-regress (will attach traces + trace ids).

Sam_g: also note calibration changes can make this worse — some quant layouts reorder KV memory for packing, which interacts badly with the kernel's memcpy assumptions. We should check quantization layout change history for the fp8 profile we rolled.

Olga_infra: agreed. I'll add a unit test in kernel-tests that runs a parity check: same request stream through fp8-vec and int8-fallback, assert KV hit parity >= 0.98 after warmup. Also adding a CI gate to block fp8-vec rollouts until parity passes for common seq distributions.

perf-bot: :rotating_light: perf-alert: model=mistral-7b profile=fp8-vec regression detected — p95 +7%, kv_hit -11% — alerted to #eng-ml

Nina_ml: thanks. For immediate mitigation, I'll patch the runtime route table to prefer int8 for routes with >40% short prefixes and roll that to canary. Can someone monitor cost impact?

Kevin_perf: will run cost delta estimate. Preliminary guess: INT8 fallback adds ~3% token cost but recovers latency and reduces error surface. I'll share numbers in the ticket.

Sam_g: FYI, attached a tiny repro harness if anyone wants to iterate quickly:```python
# repro harness snippet
for batch in [1,8]:
    run(model='mistral-7b', kernel='fp8-vec', batch=batch, trace='out.txt')
    run(model='mistral-7b', kernel='int8', batch=batch, trace='out_int8.txt')
    compare_kv_hits('out.txt','out_int8.txt')
```

Olga_infra: good. I'll pick this up after stand, add the parity CI, and try a small kernel patch to remove the strict alignment assumption. If patch is risky, we keep routing fallback until kernel fix.

Nina_ml: appreciate it. tagging @Kevin_perf for telemetry dashboards and @Sam_g for follow-up traces. :thumbsup:

Kevin_perf: noted — will add a per-route metric: `kv_hit_rate_by_kernel` and a short-term alert if drop >5% vs baseline over 5m.

Sam_g: one more note — if anyone wants raw traces: trace ids 20260318-0911-{a,b,c} (uploaded to the perf bucket).

Olga_infra: thanks, closing the loop here. Plan = (1) canary int8 routing for short prefixes, (2) CI parity test, (3) kernel alignment patch + kernel regression test, (4) rollback only if parity fails.

Kevin_perf: sounds good. I'll monitor and post numbers later today.

Nina_ml: end-to-end action items captured in ticket. Thanks all.
